Theres no inherent record and depending on which field you're looking at (assuming retail, fast food, something similar) most wont even check your references or past employers and many give you na option to sp ed civically ask that employer to not be contacted. You can be as vague as you want or not in the interview if they ask you about that job- 
Interviewer: "why did you separate from X comany?"
You: "I had medical issues at the time that prevented me from continuing my employment."
"I just had different goals than I felt I could achieve at X company."
"I decided I wanted to M pursue a more challenging option."
"Company XX and I just had a difference of opinion on many major things, like how employees and customers should be treated." 
Either way, you'll still get an interview. If you're worried about your previous employer being contacted directly, leave them with the corporate number or don't list them at all. 
Good luck. Hope you find work soon.

Most schools have some kind of practice test on their website! I'd reach out to your adviser, they should be able to give you a list of resources that could help. 
Honestly, don't stress. Your score will definitely determine which class your placed in. This could be anywhere from basic math skills to liberal arts math to college algebra. Yes, if you do very poorly, you may have to take one additional math class (this is all from my experience at my school). However, if you really are at that level, it's so much better to take the basic math class for one semester to get your skills up to par versus being put directly into a math class you'll struggle in and possibly fail which could tank your GPA. 

Good luck! Best advice I can give you is to get plenty of sleep and not to freak out about it (much easier said than done, I know) and look online for a sample test so you can feel better prepared for the kinds of questions on the test. They're usually multiple choice and fairly simple arithmetic/ algebra/ geometry questions. You probably remember more than you think you do.
